validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #74 collects eight leftovers from #61/#68: seven non-blocking review findings on the PR that hid Skip on an exhausted recurrence, and one QA finding on a pre-existing double-click defect.

The review findings are not seven unrelated bugs; they are one thing seen from seven sides. The skip-eligibility fix (scheduleIsSkippable instead of scheduleIsRecurring) shipped with a test that cannot fail without it — the reviewer reverted all four call sites to scheduleIsRecurring and `playwright test schedules.test.ts -g "hides skip"` still passed (1 passed, 23.4s), because neither e2e fixture is an exhausted recurrence, which is the only input where the two predicates differ. Around that hole the review found a self-test of the test (~50 lines asserting that a regex matches constants held in the same file), a console assertion that drives only the add path, three names that now describe half their contract, and one fixture mutated out of the describe block that owned it.

The QA finding is a separate, pre-existing defect with its own cause: SchedulesTable.tsx:225 puts onClick={() => onSelect(schedule.id)} on the whole row body and Schedules/index.tsx:120 wires onSelect={onEdit}, which dispatches pushModal. pushModal (modals/modalsSlice.ts:755) appends unconditionally — it special-cases only 'keyboard-shortcuts' — so the second click of a double-click pushes a second identical schedule-edit onto modalStack. Two live copies of the same form mount (Modals.tsx:268), useModalState's isActive compares only the top of the stack, and one Cancel pops one entry, leaving the second copy on screen.

Only one of the eight needs a product change: the double-click. The Skip behaviour itself is already correct — SchedulesTable.tsx:178 calls scheduleIsSkippable and gates Skip on it — so finding 1 is a coverage hole, not a bug. Nothing here needs a decision from a person; plan/brief.md records none, and the repo already ships both halves of the fix (the predicates, and a replaceModal reducer for exactly this stacking problem).

The previous plan for this ticket was rejected for two reasons, both of which I have checked against the source and both of which are correct. This version answers them in `debate_summary`.
validated_work_order.root_cause:
Two independent causes.

(1) Coverage, not code. The e2e test built its one-off fixture with uncheckRepeats(), whose date condition is a plain date, so scheduleIsRecurring was already false for it (that was #59's fix), and its recurring fixture was a plain never-ending monthly, for which getNextDateAfter returns a date under both predicates. The only input where scheduleIsSkippable and scheduleIsRecurring disagree — a recurrence whose endMode is after_n_occurrences and whose count has been reached — was never in the menu. The unit tests at schedules.test.ts:1056-1166 call the predicate directly, so they pass whatever the call sites do.

(2) Stack discipline. The row's onSelect is a modal opener, and it uses the appending reducer where the replacing one belongs. modalsSlice.ts exports both: pushModal appends (with a single keyboard-shortcuts special case) and replaceModal sets state.modalStack = [modal]. Nothing else on the Schedules page opens a modal from another modal, so the two reducers were indistinguishable until a user clicked twice.
validated_work_order.approach:
Six edits, in dependency order.

1. RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx — put `data-testid="recurrence-description"` on the trigger Button at :627-633. This is the handle the exhausted-recurrence fixture needs: the only way to reach the end-mode controls from a test is through the trigger, and today it is an anonymous button. No behaviour change.

2. schedule-edit-modal.ts page model — add setRecurrenceEndAfterOccurrences(occurrences?: number): open the trigger by testid, choose 'for' in #repeat_end_dropdown, and assert #end_occurrences reads '1' without typing into it. The field is uncontrolled with defaultValue={config.endOccurrences || 1} and useScheduleEdit.ts:201 seeds endOccurrences: 1, so '1' is already there; typing would go through onChangeValue and produce a string, which is how the popover's `config.endOccurrences === '1'` comparison happens to read singular today. Asserting the default instead of typing keeps that accident out of the fixture. When a count is passed, fill it, so the same helper can express the two-occurrence case.

3. schedules.test.ts — the substance of finding 1. Extend the existing test to build a third schedule through the UI: Repeats checked, the picker's end mode set to 'for' with occurrences 1, Apply, Add. Because the seed's start is today, its next date is today, its status is Due, and it is exhausted — getNextDateAfter returns null — which is exactly the discriminating input. Give it a distinct payee and no schedule name, so it is locatable by payee and so the edit path later driven over it exercises the nullable name from useScheduleEdit.ts:119. Then assert its menu equals ['Post transaction', 'Post transaction today', 'Complete', 'Delete'] — no Skip — while the never-ending monthly row keeps Skip. Both rows are located by payee, not by index, so the existing index-based assertions move past the new row. Also assert, before Apply, that the trigger re-renders as the 'once' description ('Every month on the 4th, once') and not the singular/plural 'occurrence' label.

4. schedules.test.ts, same file — delete the tautology: REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES, the loop that splits the regex on '|' and asserts each alternative has a probe, and the trailing page.evaluate that console.errors the literals back into the page. Keep reactInputWarning, CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS, watchReactInputWarnings, the drain and expect(messages).toEqual([]) — that guard is load-bearing, and the reviewer confirmed it by reverting ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134 and getting the predicted failure.

5. schedules.test.ts — drive the edit path inside the watched window (click the new row, assert the modal is open, cancel) before the console assertion, so the `fields.name ?? null` seed is exercised.

6. schedules.test.ts — new test for the QA finding: double-click a row, assert exactly one schedule-edit-modal is visible, Cancel, assert the schedules table is visible again.

7. schedules-page.ts page model — rename the three Nth methods (drop Nth, take Locator) and add editSchedule(row: number | Locator): a Locator, which opens the modal and returns a ScheduleEditModal. Menu scoping stays unscoped, matching the seven other getByRole('menu') uses in the suite; the reviewer asked for that explicitly.

8. loot-core schedules.test.ts — restore weeklyOnSaturday verbatim inside describe('getNextDateAfter') (inferred shape, no `field`, no annotation) and give describe('scheduleIsSkippable') its own factory annotated RuleConditionEntity, which necessarily carries field: 'date' because that is what scheduleIsSkippable accepts.

9. schedules/index.tsx — onEdit dispatches replaceModal instead of pushModal. onAdd, onDiscover and onChangeUpcomingLength keep pushModal; they cannot be reached twice from a row click, and ScheduleEditModal's own onEditRule push (an edit-rule modal opened from inside the form) is a different slice of the stack and is left alone.

10. A release note for the one user-visible change.

qa_script: Boot: yarn start, open http://localhost:3001, choose 'Don't use a server' then 'View demo' to load the demo budget.
Go to Schedules. Note the one pre-existing schedule (a never-ending monthly) — this is the Skip-PRESENT control, not the subject.

Open the new row's actions menu: it must offer Post transaction, Post transaction today, Complete, Delete — and no Skip. Restart being absent is expected on every non-completed row and is not part of this check.

risks: The e2e fixture depends on a start date of today: useScheduleEdit.ts seeds `start: today`, so the exhausted schedule's next date is today and its status is Due. If the test runs across midnight the row's status moves off Due; the Skip assertions do not depend on the status, but a future status assertion would.

Renaming three page-model methods touches six call sites across the schedules suite. A missed one is a typecheck failure, not a silent behaviour change, so yarn typecheck catches it before the e2e run.

replaceModal on onEdit changes stacking behaviour for every click on a Schedules row, not only double-clicks: if any code path depended on a schedule-edit modal stacking above another modal opened from this page, it would now replace it. Grepped every pushModal({ modal: { name: 'schedule-edit' — index.tsx:31 is the only one on this page; ScheduleEditModal.tsx's edit-rule push is a different modal name and is untouched.

The new fixture adds a third schedule row to a suite whose existing cases address rows by index; leaving any of them index-based would make them order-dependent and flaky. This is why the rows are located by payee.

Leaving getByRole('menu') unscoped (AC-4) keeps a latent strict-mode break: if a second role="menu" element ever mounts on a page running this suite, the wait in openScheduleMenu throws. That is a deliberate, reviewer-directed choice for repo consistency, and it is listed in out_of_scope rather than fixed here.
The e2e suite lengthens by two journeys (a full create-through-the-picker fixture and a double-click), adding to an already slow file.
out_of_scope: Scoping getByRole('menu') repo-wide across accounts, budget, payees, rules, reports and schedules. Finding 7's own instruction is 'if you do scope it, scope it repo-wide in one pass rather than only here', and this ticket does not otherwise touch those files.
A shared e2e warning-probe helper housing the Radix dialog probe alongside any React probe. Finding 2 says that self-check belongs there, out of scope for this ticket.

Comparing all four skip-eligibility menus against each other. Finding 1 notes that nothing today would catch a fifth skip site — true, but that is a consequence of the fix rather than one of this ticket's eight items, and it reaches into the transaction menu surfaces this ticket does not otherwise touch.

Changing the popover's 'occurrence'/'occurrences' label. It is correctly singular today only by way of the uncontrolled field's string value; whether it should be 'occurrence' or 'occurrences' at 1 is a copy decision, and the test asserts what the trigger renders rather than touching what the popover renders.
Debouncing or otherwise rate-limiting the Schedules row's onClick. The stacking is a reducer-choice bug and replaceModal already exists to express 'this modal replaces what is open'.
Anything about the recurring-date description's wording or formatting beyond exposing its existing string to a test.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every claim in this order was checked against the source at a named line, and both reasons the last plan was rejected were verified as correct rather than argued with — the demo budget genuinely has no exhausted recurrence (one schedule, a never-ending monthly, confirmed by unzipping the committed fixture and querying it), and the trigger genuinely renders 'once' (schedule.ts:57-61, already asserted at util/schedule.test.ts:256). The single product change is a one-token reducer swap with an existing reducer for the purpose and a single caller on the page. The residual risk is concentrated in the e2e fixture, which is why it is built through the UI the reviewer prescribed rather than seeded, and why AC-8 exists to prove the new tests fail without the fixes.
evidence: The demo budget is the QA browser's starting state: unzipping packages/desktop-client/e2e/data/actual-demo-budget.zip and running `select count(*) from schedules` returns 1, and that row's rule condition is {"op":"isapprox","field":"date","value":{"start":"2023-02-28","frequency":"monthly","patterns":[]}} — no endMode, no exhausted recurrence, and nothing reading 'once'. This is the direct reason the rejected AC-1's procedure presupposed a row that is not on the page.

util/schedule.ts:57-61 renders t('once') for endMode 'after_n_occurrences' when endOccurrences === 1 and t('{{endOccurrences}} times') otherwise; util/schedule.test.ts:256 already asserts 'Every 2 weeks on Monday, once'. The singular/plural label lives at RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:461 and is rendered only while the popover is open. The rejected plan asserted 'occurrence' in six places, which no rendered trigger ever produces.

SchedulesTable.tsx:178 computes `const canSkip = scheduleIsSkippable(dateCond, schedule.next_date)` and is the only gate on Skip; the Skip item is hidden when status === 'completed' || !canSkip. Restart, at :186, is hidden for status !== 'completed' — so on a Due row it is absent whatever the recurrence does, and it cannot be part of an exhaustion contrast.

validated_work_order.debate_summary:
The previous plan (v2) was rejected with two numbered objections. Both are correct on the source, and this plan takes the remedies each names rather than defending the old text.

Objection 1 — AC-1's how_to_verify presupposed a row that is not on the page. The recipe said to open the actions menu on a schedule whose recurring date reads 'for 1 occurrence'. I unzipped the committed demo budget (packages/desktop-client/e2e/data/actual-demo-budget.zip) and queried it: one schedule, rule condition {op:'isapprox', field:'date', value:{start:'2023-02-28', frequency:'monthly', patterns:[]}} — no endMode, no exhausted recurrence, and no string reading 'occurrence' anywhere. The objection stands. I take the reviewer's option (a): AC-1 keeps verify:"browser" and its recipe now CREATES the subject — Add new schedule, Repeats, end mode 'for', occurrences 1, Apply, Add — before asserting on it, using the app's own seeded start of today so the row is Due and exhausted. The reviewer also warned not to weaken the clause that makes AC-1 discriminate. It is not weakened: the contrast is exhausted-has-no-Skip versus never-ending-has-Skip, and I have explicitly removed Restart from the contrast, because SchedulesTable.tsx:186 hides it for every non-completed row — its absence would be true of any Due schedule and would discriminate nothing.

Objection 2 — six locations asserted the string 'occurrence' where the trigger renders 'once'. Correct: schedule.ts:57-61 emits t('once') for a one-occurrence end mode, util/schedule.test.ts:256 already fixes the rendered string as 'Every month on Monday, once', and the singular/plural label is a separate control at RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:461 that only exists while the popover is open. All six are corrected. files[3].change (a) now asserts the trigger reads the 'once' description after Apply, and tests[0].cases[1] asserts the same; the page-model helper deliberately leaves #end_occurrences at the app's seeded 1 rather than typing into it, so the fixture does not depend on the uncontrolled field's string value, which is the accident that makes the popover's label read singular today.

The reviewer also said the recurrence-description testid addition itself is sound and should stay, so files[1] changes nothing else. The remaining five findings and QA's finding are carried forward as written, with finding 7's explicit instruction (leave getByRole('menu') unscoped for consistency) preferred over finding 4's, and the repo-wide scoping pass it points at listed in out_of_scope rather than half-done here.
residual_risks: The exhausted-recurrence fixture is the ticket's load-bearing test and it is a long UI journey; a future change to the picker's layout or the RecurConfig shape breaks it in a way that reads as a test failure rather than a product one.

Deleting the probe self-check leaves the two React warning literals unverified against a future React upgrade — but they are React's own wording, and the reviewer is right that the constant beside the regex proves nothing about the app.
